summary: King County, WA tower site (30-ft pole platform 1928/29; 20-ft DNR tower 1950) torn down 1966; a 20-ft replica was built in 2021 on the summit.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden DNR tower with 14x14 live-in cab, built 1950; the register says 40 ft (disputed)
facts.status_note: Original torn down May 13, 1966; a 20-foot replica with a viewing platform and windowless cab was built in 2021 and is open on Mount Peak
facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR (site now King County Parks)

staffing.status: Original tower last manned full-time in 1964 and manned four days in 1965; the replica is not staffed for fire detection

access.note: King County park; the trail is well used and the replica is open to visitors per WTA (November 2021)

visit.trail_note: Hike from the south trailhead off SE Mud Mountain Road (gravel lot, bathrooms). WTA gives about 3.6 miles and about 1,200 ft of gain from there; a visitor page gives 1 to 2 miles depending on the route.

events.note: 30-ft pole platform tower (register and firelookout.com). A visitor page dates the tower to May 1929, built by the Washington Forest Fire Association. The year is disputed.
A higher 60-ft tower put up by the Washington Forest Fire Association (visitor page only; no other source read mentions it)
20-ft wooden DNR tower with 14x14 live-in cab (visitor page and FFLA 2018 report). firelookout.com says 1949 for a 20-ft L-4 tower; the register says a 40-ft tower.
Last manned full-time in 1964; abandoned October 16 that year
Manned four days in March 1965 (March 13, 14, 20 and 21)
Torn down May 13, 1966 with a D-4 tractor after vandalism and break-ins. firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1966'. The register gives 1971 (disputed).
FFLA restoration grant of $500 toward rebuilding a historically accurate replica of the 20-ft DNR tower
20-ft replica with viewing platform and windowless cab (firelookout.com); in place and open on Mount Peak per a November 2021 WTA trip report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1928 for the 30-ft pole platform tower; a visitor page says the Washington Forest Fire Association built it in May 1929. The story gives both.

The visitor page and the 2018 FFLA report give a 20-ft tower built in 1950; firelookout.com gives a 20-ft L-4 tower in 1949; the register gives a 40-ft tower. The story follows the 1950, 20-ft version and notes the others.
Three sources give 1966 (visitor page, FFLA 2018 report, firelookout.com); the register gives 1971. The story uses 1966 and notes the register.
A visitor page gives 1 or 2 miles depending on route; WTA gives about 3.6 miles from the south trailhead. The story gives both with their sources.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 'replica planned' is out of date: the replica was built in 2021 and open by November 2021. The register (firetower.org) is the outlier on height (40 ft), the 1950 date and the 1971 removal year; FFLOS may want to review its entry. Search snippets (not read, not cited) mention a 2021 King County partnership to restore the Mt. Peak fire lookout and a 2021 Courier-Herald article on the replica; those could name the builder or sponsor, which no source read names. The handmade replica model displayed in the DNR building lobby in Enumclaw (visitor page, undated) is not a standing structure and is not described in the story beyond this note. Access is recorded as public (King County park).
